findings.body:
**Replace the complete `ExecStart` directive.**

Systemd allows a directive to continue onto the next physical line. A wrapped `ExecStart` passes the one-match check at Line 594, but Line 427 replaces only its first line. This leaves the old continuation in the generated unit even though the returned `exec_start` shows the new command. Replace the full logical directive, or reject wrapped `ExecStart` directives when selecting Node. Preserve the Python render. ([freedesktop.org](https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/256/systemd.syntax.html?utm_source=openai))
findings.title: Replace the complete `ExecStart` directive.

findings.body:
**Refuse a preview that would overwrite its input overlay.**

If the operator supplies `config.json` as the overlay and selects its directory as `--output`, Line 873 replaces the overlay with the rendered runner config. The preview can report success, but the next invocation rejects that file because it no longer has the overlay schema. Reject an output path that aliases the overlay before writing the audit or preview files.
findings.title: Refuse a preview that would overwrite its input overlay.

findings.body:
**Prevent checkout from overwriting ignored host files.**

If the target starts tracking a path that contains an ignored host-local file, Line 773 does not report the file. Git can silently replace it at Line 782. The post-switch status then passes because the replacement matches the target. Use `--no-overwrite-ignore` on the forward and rollback checkouts so a collision stops the checkout rather than discarding local data. ([git-scm.com](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-checkout?utm_source=openai))
findings.title: Prevent checkout from overwriting ignored host files.

findings.body:
**Reject inconclusive Git location checks.**

Line 205 treats every nonzero Git exit as proof that the path is outside Git. If Git refuses to inspect a shared checkout because of ownership, `record()` can still write a private audit file inside that checkout. Reject probe failures unless the check establishes that no repository contains the path. ([git-scm.com](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-config?utm_source=openai))
findings.title: Reject inconclusive Git location checks.

findings.body:
**Render launchd templates from the recorded commit.**

If a tracked plist has an uncommitted edit, Lines 672–673 include that edit in the preview. The audit names `HEAD`, and the config and systemd output come from committed blobs. Resolve one SHA for the preview and use it to enumerate and read the launchd templates as well as to render and record the other outputs.
findings.title: Render launchd templates from the recorded commit.

findings.body:
**Check the resolved preview subdirectories before writing.**

Lines 867–869 check the output directory but not its `systemd` and `launchd` children. If either child is a symlink into the deployment checkout, the renderer follows it and can replace checkout files. Validate the actual output directories before writing any preview artifacts. Reject destinations that resolve inside a Git checkout.
findings.title: Check the resolved preview subdirectories before writing.

findings.body:
**Implement the machine-mode CLI contract.**

Line 853 rejects `--json` before dispatch. If an ordinary invocation cannot read its overlay, Lines 885–887 emit only a stderr message. Add machine-mode handling before argument parsing so usage errors and operation failures each produce one JSON artifact, leave stderr empty, and use the required exit code. Keep narration on stderr in normal mode.

As per coding guidelines, “In machine mode (`--json`) stderr stays empty” and “stdout is still exactly one JSON artifact.”






Also applies to: 878-879, 885-887
findings.title: Implement the machine-mode CLI contract.

findings.body:
**Make the switch refuse while a `crq-repair.service` start job is queued.**

`switch()` and its stopped-state check read only `ActiveState`. A unit with a queued start job still reports `inactive`, so the check passes while that job waits. The manual helper path does not set the handover marker, so the queued job can start during the checkout. The service then imports checkout modules and reads `config.json` before any refusal, and it can dispatch paid work. The approved driver path claims `state/runner-disabled` before it stops units. That marker stops dispatch before the config read, but not before the import-time reads.

Require the switch to refuse while any `crq-*` job is queued or running, or otherwise keep a queued `crq-repair.service` start from running during the hold. The mechanism is open: query the job queue, require the marker on the manual path, or cancel the job. Whichever mechanism is chosen must cover the manual helper path as well as the driver.
findings.title: Make the switch refuse while a `crq-repair.service` start job is queued.

findings.body:
**Check `.upholds` directories for foreign enablement links.**

On systemd v257, a link in `ingress.target.upholds/` can make `ingress.target` restart `crq-tick.service` whenever the service becomes inactive. Line 856 checks only `.wants` and `.requires`. The dependency scanner reads the link target as a declared fragment, so it can report `supported=True` without detecting the link itself. Apply the undeclared-link check to `.upholds` directories too. ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/systemd/systemd/v257/src/core/load-dropin.c))
findings.title: Check `.upholds` directories for foreign enablement links.

findings.body:
**Refuse dependency-directory symlinks that discovery cannot inspect.**

If `ingress.target.wants` points to a directory containing a link to `crq-tick.service`, systemd v257 resolves the directory and loads the dependency. The non-following probe and the recursive scanner both skip the directory, so discovery can return `complete=True` and `supported=True`. Keep the no-follow policy, but return a refusal for an unexamined dependency-directory symlink instead of treating it as absent. ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/systemd/systemd/v257/src/shared/dropin.c))
findings.title: Refuse dependency-directory symlinks that discovery cannot inspect.

findings.body:
**Compare complete dependency names, not substrings.**

If `ingress.service` declares `Wants=backup-crq-tick.service`, `findall` extracts `crq-tick.service`. Discovery then rejects the selected topology even though the dependency names a different service. Parse complete unit-name arguments before comparing them with `expected`. A direct `Wants=crq-tick.service` must still be rejected for this cotenant. ([freedesktop.org](https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/256/systemd.unit.html?utm_source=openai))
findings.title: Compare complete dependency names, not substrings.

findings.body:
**Enforce the entry budget before collecting directory contents.**

A single `.wants` directory can contain far more than `MAX_SCAN_ENTRIES`. Line 858 collects every child, and Line 863 sorts the full list before the bounded dependency walk runs. Line 547 has the same problem for declared drop-ins. Apply a cumulative budget during enumeration. For declared drop-ins, reject the first unexpected name instead of collecting and sorting every entry.







Also applies to: 858-858
findings.title: Enforce the entry budget before collecting directory contents.
